testsuite.name: com.systemwebstudio.publish.ReleaseScopeLeaseTests

testcase.name: two workers racing for one scope - exactly one wins, every time()
the heartbeat keeps a working operation's lease alive beyond its TTL()
a higher activation number goes on, and a rollback after it is newer still()
lease expiry - another operation takes over, the dead worker's pointer write is refused, the new owner's is not()
a lower activation number is stale - it never activates and the scope is given straight back()
the old holder releasing late does not release the new holder's scope()
publish A is slow, its lease expires, B takes over and publishes, A finishes late - A is fenced out and B stays active()
one operation owns the scope at a time - the second is told who holds it, and gets it after the release()
without a heartbeat the lease expires after its TTL and can be taken()
the same operation takes the scope again after a crash - it gets a NEW fencing token, resumes, and the earlier thread of it is fenced out()
the same activation number resumes only for the SAME operation()
a commit that carries a step writes both or neither()
taking the scope inside a caller's open transaction neither blocks others nor is blocked - every statement is its own transaction()
the maximum lifetime is respected - a heartbeat cannot keep a runaway operation alive for ever()
an operation of another tenant or another app cannot take the scope()
the pointer commit is a compare-and-set - the version moves by one, an outdated version is refused()
higher activation number with a stale fencing token is refused - the number alone grants nothing()
